transliteration:
pitṛputravivādaś ca prāyaścittavyatikramaḥ
pratigrahavilopaś ca kopa āśramiṇām api
sph_interpretive_translation: Conflict between father and son arises due to neglect of expiation; loss of acceptance leads to anger even among renunciants.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through conscious alignment, not biological lineage alone
Causation originates in failure to perform corrective action (prāyaścitta)
Capacity-based responsibility requires inner stability before external duty
Restoration logic demands purification of relational fields prior to judgment
Consciousness alignment prevents degradation of spiritual station
executable_legal_axioms: IF relational conflict occurs THEN initiate prāyaścitta completion process BEFORE adjudication
IF pratigraha (acceptance) is withdrawn THEN underlying spiritual imbalance must be addressed
IF anger manifests in sannyasa THEN assess vyatikrama (neglect of dharma) as primary cause
IF familial discord reported THEN evaluate causal chain: prāyaścitta → pratigraha → emotional equilibrium
IF ashram dweller exhibits agitation THEN bypass punitive measures and restore śama-sadhana protocols
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, conflicts involving family or renunciants shall not proceed to verdict until prāyaścitta adherence status is verified. Emotional disturbance in any party indicates vyatikrama requiring restoration, not litigation.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that anger stems from unresolved inner transaction (pratigraha-vilopa). Anupūrvaśaḥ establishes that neglect of prāyaścitta precedes relational breakdown. Therefore, proportional responsibility lies in restoring internal order rather than assigning blame. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that suffering arises from misalignment, not misconduct.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate prāyaścitta rectification protocol for all involved parties
Re-establish pratigraha through guided acceptance completion process
Implement śama-prakriyā (emotional equanimity procedures) for agitated individuals
Activate dharmic field restoration using collective sankalpa alignment
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam: Conflict originates in spiritual neglect, not moral failure. Dharma is restored through consciousness realignment. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness remains the supreme adjudicator.
